key_idea: By Lucas' theorem C(n,k) is not divisible by p exactly when every base-p digit of k is at most the matching digit of n, so the non-divisible count is the product of (digit+1).
sketch: Write n in base p with digits d_i; the number of k in [0,n] with p not dividing C(n,k) is prod(d_i+1). The answer is (n+1) minus that product. O(log_p n). The product never exceeds n+1 <= 1e18+1, so unsigned 64-bit is safe; n=0 gives 0. The n/p <= 1e6 bound in the statement is a red herring suggesting a slower intended solution. Verified against brute force for all n<80 and several primes.
